This can occur either from insufficient insulin production (type 1 diabetes) or resistance to insulin (type 2 diabetes). 

Symptoms of diabetes may include frequent urination, increased thirst, unexplained weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision, slow healing wounds, and increased risk of infections. If left untreated, it can lead to complications such as heart disease, kidney damage, nerve damage, and eye problems.

The diagnosis of diabetes often involves a combination of physical examination, blood tests (e.g., fasting plasma glucose, hemoglobin A1c), and sometimes a urine test. In some cases, an oral glucose tolerance test might be performed to differentiate between type 1 and type 2.

Treatment for diabetes typically includes lifestyle changes like a balanced diet, regular exercise, and proper weight management. For type 1, insulin injections or an insulin pump are necessary.
